approach: (1) FRESH-VM triage at the exact tip 13d5c0d781d28228ab95d60760e5e018d283083a (VM njhd3smdzagqt7qdj6bhmw36, rust:1-bookworm 8c/32GB/100GB - the gate pool's exact image/spec, toolchain 1.98.1 pinned): solo x5 RELEASE + x5 DEBUG of the single test; then the full-suite co-scheduled context x2 (cargo +1.98.1 test --workspace --no-fail-fast with the gate env parity: /opt/kernel-venv seeded runtime+skills, PRIME_AGENT_KERNEL_PYTHON/PA_E2E_KERNEL_PYTHON/PI_PACKAGE_DIR, CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0) to characterize any residual co-scheduling rate. verdict: (b) ENVIRONMENTAL DNS red - the authoritative renewal. The mcp_login worker_begin_login red is the DNS failure mode: the test resolves the bare name 'localhost' once per run at the simulated-browser redirect; pooled gate VMs whose image-build shipped a NUL-padded /etc/hosts have no files leg, and the DNS fallback NXDOMAINs the bare name, so getaddrinfo returns 'failed to lookup address information: Name or service not known'. NOT a code red (10/10 solo green at tip 13d5c0d781d28228ab95d60760e5e018d283083a, release + debug); NOT a co-scheduling flake (the 09-25 registration's family assignment is falsified by the per-VM era timeline + the single-signature census + the healthy-resolver co-scheduled evidence); CI never fails it (healthy runner resolvers + 0 failures in the scanned window). Registration RENEWED with the corrected class, the full evidence, the DNS environmental trigger, and the reopen trigger; expiry 2026-09-29. Standing remedy (operator-owned): the /etc/hosts overwrite at gate bootstrap/pool claim - until applied, both pooled gate VMs remain deterministically red on this test and the renewed registration auto-classifies those reds.

dns_dependency_map.what_the_test_resolves: The bare name 'localhost' - the OAuth callback redirect_uri is http://localhost:<53700+offset>/callback (crates/pa-core/src/mcp/oauth_callback.rs redirect_uri_for); the test parses the recorded authorization URL, strips the scheme and /callback, and drives tokio::net::TcpStream::connect("localhost:<port>") to land the simulated browser redirect (crates/pa-daemon/src/mcp_login.rs, the client side). The callback LISTENER binds PI_OAUTH_CALLBACK_HOST (default 127.0.0.1 - numeric, no DNS on the server side); the scripted transport covers discovery/registration/token (no network); resolution happens EXACTLY ONCE per run, at the redirect step.
dns_dependency_map.when: after the login task spawns and the authorization URL is recorded (10s file deadline), before the credential persist + gating asserts
dns_dependency_map.why_pooled_gate_vms_hit_name_or_service_: The fleet gate pool VMs (ykp6mbwtdtz17w58tayfa0yw slot-0, bvwr5lk9t7jbsj3e5tc6x7im slot-1, both created from rust:1-bookworm 2026-09-24/25) ship /etc/hosts as 59 NUL BYTES (od -c: zero-filled; stat mtime = image-build time 2026-09-24, never modified since) - the FILES leg is deterministically unparseable, so getent hosts localhost fails rc=2. nsswitch is 'hosts: files dns' with resolv.conf nameserver 8.8.8.8; the DNS fallback NXDOMAINs the bare single-label name ('localhost.' rcode=3, live 50/50 to 8.8.8.8 + 20/20 to 1.1.1.1). With BOTH legs failing, getaddrinfo returns EAI_NONAME = 'failed to lookup address information: Name or service not known' - the exact one-line failure in all 58 fleet run logs. The fresh VM created 2026-09-27 ships a WELL-FORMED 59-byte /etc/hosts ('127.0.0.1 localhost' + '192.0.2.1 prime.internal') - the platform's image-build intermittently writes the NUL-padded file (same 59-byte size), which is the environmental trigger. The green ERAS on the pooled VMs (slot-1 through 2026-09-25 01:39; slot-0 through 2026-09-26 23:47, ~35 consecutive full gates) are the DNS leg answering the bare name - the answer flips per VM over time (slot-1 flipped ~03:36-04:06 09-25, slot-0 flipped 00:05 09-27), independent of code heads and of co-scheduling load.
dns_dependency_map.standing_remedy: Overwrite (never append) /etc/hosts with '127.0.0.1 localhost\n::1 localhost\n' at gate bootstrap/pool claim - the proven recipe since 2026-09-23 (r1-finish lane memory). OPERATOR-OWNED: the fleet driver (fleet-tools/fleet_pipeline.py BOOTSTRAP/READY_CHECK or the pool-claim path) does not touch /etc/hosts today; both pool VMs are currently hard-red for this test until patched or recreated. GitHub CI runners have healthy /etc/hosts, so the files leg always resolves - the test cannot fail this way in CI.
